senses.gloss: f. (also אִסְטָרָא m.) cacophemistic appellations of all kinds of gentile sports; cmp. the use of θέατρον and θεατρίζειν in Ad Corinth. I, IV, 9, a. Hebr. X, 33; אסטריא &c., as if a denomin. of סרר, cmp. Syr. אסטרניא, אצטרניא, P. Sm. 304 a. cit. ibid.; אצטריבא, as if fr. צרב; אצטרדיון (v. next w.) as if fr. צרד, v. אִיצְטַדִּין; cmp. אֲבֵידָן) theatre, arena, gladiatorial shows, &c.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Avodah Zarah 1:7">Ab. Zar. I, 7</cite> (<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 16a:13">16ᵃ</cite>) <he>גרדום אצטדייא וכ׳</he> (Ms. M. <he>אצטריבא</he>, but in Ib. 18ᵇ repeatedly <cite ref="A02871"><he>אצטריא</he></cite>; Y. ed. <he>איסטדייא</he>; Mish. Nap. <cite ref="A02865"><he>אצטדיא</he></cite>, comment. <he>אצטרדיא</he>) place of execution, of shows &c.; v. Ib. 18ᵇ.—[<cite ref="Menachot 103b:20">Men. 103ᵇ</cite> <he>איסטריא של מלך</he> the king’s amphitheatre, v. <cite ref="A02412"><he>אסטרטיא</he></cite>]. Pl. <cite ref="A02350"><he>אִסְטַרְיוֹת</he></cite>. Sifra Aḥaré <cite ref="Mishnah Parah 9">Par. IX</cite> ch. 13. Tanḥ.
